After a year of dormancy, Cosmos 2504 did a close approach with a piece of Chinese space debris from the 2007 ASAT test; Possibly part of Nivelir program used for intelligence & space situational awareness

Cosmos 2521 separated from Cosmos 2519 and performed a series of small maneuvers to do inspections before 
redocking with Cosmos 2519. Cosmos 2523 separated from Cosmos 2521 but did not maneuver on its own.
Cosmos 2521 conducted close approaches of Cosmos 2519.

In September 2019, Russia's Luch (OLYMP) satellite approached China's TJS-3 satellite within 30 kilometers. This approach took place several weeks after the launch of TJS-3. This event was reported to be the first instance of an event between a manueverable Russian satellite and a maneuverable Chinese satellite.
Cosmos 2535 and Cosmos 2536 conducted at least 25 individual RPO operations to within 2 km and as far apart as 380 km. Debris created

Cosmos 2542 deployed an inspector subsatellite; Cosmos 2543 raised its orbit to come within 30 km of USA 245 (NRO KH-11 satellite) and established repeated close approaches within 150 km, likely for the purpose of surveillance; Cosmos 2542 also made close approaches to USD 245; Possibly part of Nivelir program used for intelligence & space situational awareness
Cosmos 2543 rendezvoused with Cosmos 2535 and released a small object at high relative velocity; In Sept, Cosmos 2536 joined in the RPO with the other two and may have docked with Cosmos 2535.
Cosmos 2558 has matched the orbital plane of USA 326 and conducted repeat close approaches, getting within 50 km of USA 326 once a week
Resurs-P3 was presumed inactive after failed solar panel deployment, but maneuevered to raise its orbit and was then approached by Cosmos 2562 for an RPO.

Cosmos 2570 released another satellite, Cosmos 2571. After circularizing, Cosmos 2571 once again released a third satellite, catalogued as Object D in late November. Commercial satellite tracking firm LeoLabs reported that Object D had maneuvered and performed at least one close pass of Cosmos 2571, potentially as part of an imaging attempt.
Luch 2 parked near several satellites including American WGS F2 and multiple European commercial communications satellites.

Close apporach manuevers and inspection of other satellites; Sponsored by USAF, possible co-orbital ASAT test/investigation
DART did a series of autonomous maneuvers to bring it close to the MUBLCOM satellite and ended up bumping into it.

DARPA demonstration of autonomous on-orbit techniques with two satellites including refueling; Servicing mission; yet, run by the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency – possible military precussor/application
Inspection and close rendevous with a failed US satellite; Possibly other demonstrations and tests in geosynchronous orbit

USA 202 drifted westward around 0.8 degrees per day for several weeks, and eventually stabilized in a geosynchronous orbit at 44 degrees east longitude in May 2009. That placement put it right next to commercial satellite Thuraya 2, where it appeared to match up with the latter’s orbital inclination.

Part of NROs Nemesis satellites (geostationary COMINT); Presuumed to have completed SIGNIT (signals intelligence) with other satellites; Unique for roaming various times to different orbits and satellites

Part of NROs Nemesis satellites (geostationary COMINT); Similar to PAN with classified communications surveillance and rotating between different orbits; Worked on "targeting commercial satellite uplinks" of foreign satellites
RPO demonstrations, using electro-optical sensors to gain intelligence on other satellites; Expected 6 satellites in total as part of the Hornet series by 2020
RPO demonstrations in GSO disposal region, satellite inspection
Mycroft payload deployed from Eagle Satellite, Mycroft RPO of Eagle in GEO region, satellite inspection
Mycroft manuevered to rendevous with S5 after S5 ceased communications
On August 2020, USA 271 approached the PRC's SJ-20, shadowing the spacecraft. The Chinese spacecraft detected the U.S. satellite and rapidly moved away.

In January 2022, USA 270 drifted near China's Shiyan-12(01) and (02) satellites just below the GEO belt. The USA 270 got close, pulled a maneuver and within 2 days, the Shiyan-12 satellites had left the vicinity. The closest approach was around 73 kilometers.
In October 2024, LDPE 3A maneuvered to approach SJ-23, possibly to 30 km by Nov. 4 or Nov. 5, after which it maneuvered to synchronize itself with SJ-23.

BX-1 was deployed from SZ-7 and proceeded to orbit around the spacecraft; “BX-1 may have been designed to test in-orbit ejection of “companion” satellites, dual-use on-orbit inspection capabilities, 
and use of attitude control and propulsion systems for formation flying"
SJ-12 moved to rendevous with SJ-O6F and may have bumped it

SY-7 released an additional object that it performed maneuvers with and may have had a telerobotic arm. CX-3 performed optical surveillance of other in-space objects. SJ-15 Demonstrated altitude and inclination changes to approach other satellites.; Some space debris observations; In Dec 2015, SJ-15 raised orbit to CX-3 demonstrating multi-orbit inspection

YZ-2 upper stage failed to burn to the graveyard orbit and stayed near GEO. SJ-17 demonstrated maneuverability around 
the GEO belt and circumnavigated Chinasat 5A.
TJS-3 AGM separated from TJS-3 in GEO and both manuevered slightly to stay within close orbits
TJS-3 is drifting around the GEO belt, periodically stopping to approach Russian and US satellites; from Nov. 2023- Nov. 2024, it conducted RPOs with TJS-10; it then started moving again

SJ-17 made smaller changes to RPO with Chinasat 6B in January 2020 and, SJ-20, a new Chinese high bandwidth 
communications satellite launched in December 2019, in October 2020
SJ-21 maneuvered to dock with Compass G2 and pull it into a much higher orbit.

USA 270 maneuvered to approach SY-12 01 and SY-12 02. The two Chinese satellites made significant maneuvers to split up and begin rotating around the GEO belt in opposite directions, with SY-12 02 apparently also getting an imaging opportunity on USA 270.
PRC Test Spacecraft 2 (Shenlong spaceplane) released Object J and made multiple RPOs, including repeated docking, deployment, and formation flying.
SJ-17 made a brief RPO with VENESAT-1, a Venezuelan communications satellite built and launched by China in 2008

In June 2024, China's experimental spaceplane (PRC Test Spacecraft 3) conducted an RPO with another Chinese spacecraft "Object G." Object G was released into orbit by the spaceplane on May 14, 2024, and between June 5 - 8, PRC Test Spacecraft 3 carried out a series of avoidance maneuvers and approaches with the object.
